claims.claim: spark.sql.shuffle.partitions defaults to 200; createDataFrame with only column names infers types and fails on all-None columns.
claims.source: Run on PySpark 4.0.4 in this repository.

claims.claim: configure_spark_with_delta_pip adds the Delta package matching the installed delta-spark version.

concept_html:
Unit tests for PySpark run on your laptop and in CI, not on a cluster. A local session that starts in seconds and runs small jobs fast needs a few settings:

builder = (
    SparkSession.builder.master("local[2]")
    .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "2")
    .config("spark.ui.enabled", "false")
    .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
    .config("spark.sql.sources.default", "delta")
)
spark = configure_spark_with_delta_pip(builder).getOrCreate()
  • local[2] runs Spark in one process with two worker threads. Two threads, not one, so bugs that depend on partitioning still show up.
  • spark.sql.shuffle.partitions defaults to 200. On ten test rows, every shuffle creates 200 tiny tasks. Two is plenty.
  • configure_spark_with_delta_pip from delta-spark adds the matching Delta JAR. The two config lines enable Delta SQL and the Delta catalog.
  • Open-source Spark writes saveAsTable as Parquet by default. Databricks uses Delta. Set the default so tests behave like production.

Test data. Build it with an explicit schema, as a DDL string such as "respondent_id STRING, final_weight DOUBLE". Inference guesses types from values, fails on a column of only None (CANNOT_DETERMINE_TYPE), and turns 2 into a LONG where production has DOUBLE.

A test data builder keeps tests short: one function returns a valid row with sensible defaults, and each test overrides only the field it is about.

def respondent(**overrides: object) -> dict[str, object]:
    row = {"respondent_id": "R1", "wave_id": "W1", "final_weight": 1.0, "in_scope": True}
    row.update(overrides)
    return row

A test that says respondent(final_weight=None) tells the reader exactly what it is testing.

lines: RESPONDENT_SCHEMA = "respondent_id STRING, wave_id STRING, final_weight DOUBLE, in_scope BOOLEAN"
def respondent(**overrides: object) -> dict[str, object]:
"""A valid silver respondent. Override only the fields a test is about."""
row: dict[str, object] = {"respondent_id": "R1", "wave_id": "W1", "final_weight": 1.0, "in_scope": True}
unknown = set(overrides) - set(row)
if unknown:
raise KeyError(f"unknown fields: {sorted(unknown)}")
row.update(overrides)
return row
def respondents_df(spark: SparkSession, rows: list[dict[str, object]]) -> DataFrame:
"""DataFrame with the silver schema, whatever the values."""
fields = [f.split()[0] for f in RESPONDENT_SCHEMA.split(", ")]
return spark.createDataFrame([tuple(r[f] for f in fields) for r in rows], RESPONDENT_SCHEMA)
def test_null_weights_are_reported(spark: SparkSession) -> None:
df = respondents_df(spark, [respondent(), respondent(respondent_id="R2", final_weight=None)])
assert null_weight_count(df) == 1

notes.html: One DDL schema: types match production, and None is always allowed.
A typo such as final_wieght fails loudly instead of silently adding nothing.
The test reads as its intent: a second respondent with a missing weight.

example.takeaway_html: A tuned local session makes tests fast enough to run on every change. Builders with explicit schemas make them short and exact.

title: A fast local SparkSession and readable test data
why_html:
A project's Spark tests take 14 minutes in CI, so developers stop running them locally. The session uses the default 200 shuffle partitions, and each of the 60 tests runs two or three shuffles on a handful of rows. Most of the time goes into scheduling empty tasks. A MERGE bug that a test would have caught ships to production, because nobody waited for the suite.

With local[2] and two shuffle partitions, the same suite runs in under two minutes, and people run it before every push.
